purpose: machine-readable ontology for selecting, justifying, and validating research designs that align question, paradigm, sampling, validity, and ethics, as a subdomain node of research methodology and epistemology for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: Research Design is modeled as a subdomain of research methodology and epistemology.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable design work units, decision areas, or validity/ethics controls.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope follows Creswell & Creswell (2018) and Shadish, Cook & Campbell (2002) framing of design, validity, and inference.
exclusions: Detailed statistical estimation and modeling techniques (analysis stage, not design).
Data management, fieldwork logistics, and project scheduling.

competency_questions.question: Given a research question and unit of analysis, which design type's inference logic can validly answer it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RQ_DESIGN_ALIGN maps question typology to design

competency_questions.question: Which epistemological paradigm grounds the chosen methods and is it consistent with them?
How is the design family (quantitative/qualitative/mixed) chosen and when are strands integrated?
What licenses a causal claim and how do experimental vs quasi-experimental designs differ?
Which internal-validity threats apply to a design, how are they controlled, and how does this trade against generalizability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTERNAL_VALIDITY and EXTERNAL_VALIDITY present with tradeoff

competency_questions.question: How is selection bias addressed when randomization is impossible?
When is an observational or survey design appropriate and what are its inferential limits?
Which qualitative design fits an in-depth contextual or theory-building question, and how is saturation determined?
Does the question require a cross-sectional snapshot or a longitudinal structure, and how does that affect ordering and attrition?
Which sampling strategy matches the design and inference goal?
Is the study adequately powered (or saturated) for the smallest meaningful effect, and how are statistical conclusions protected?
To whom and where do the findings generalize and what bounds the claim?
Do the measures validly and reliably represent the intended constructs?
What ethical and IRB requirements gate the design before data collection?

glossary.definition: the overall plan linking research questions to data collection and analysis logic
degree to which an observed effect is attributable to the studied variable rather than confounds
degree to which findings generalize across populations, settings, and times
degree to which a measure or manipulation represents the intended theoretical construct
correctness of inferences about covariation given power, assumptions, and error control
consistency and low measurement error of an instrument or rating
a comparative design with controls but without random assignment
random selection from a frame giving each unit a known nonzero selection probability
selecting cases to develop emerging theory until saturation
point at which additional data yields no new categories or insight
repeated measurement of the same units over time
intentional integration of quantitative and qualitative strands for joint inference

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established research-design and validity literature (e.g., Creswell & Creswell 2018; Shadish, Cook & Campbell 2002) and methodological practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Translate the research question, aims, and hypotheses into the design type whose logic of inference can actually answer them.
contradictors: method-first researcher who fixes design before the question

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the research question is reframed from descriptive to causal or vice versa

pros.claim: baseline decision all later design choices inherit
pros.example: a causal 'does X cause Y' question forces a comparative/experimental logic, not a single-group survey

cons.claim: misalignment here invalidates every downstream method choice
cons.example: running a cross-sectional survey to answer a causal question yields un-interpretable associations

failure_modes: causal question answered with purely correlational design
unit of analysis mismatched to the claim
acceptance_tests: each aim maps to a design whose inference logic supports it
unit of analysis stated and consistent with hypotheses

nodes.definition: Choose and justify the worldview (positivist, post-positivist, constructivist, pragmatist, transformative) that grounds the design's assumptions about knowledge and reality.
contradictors: naive empiricist who treats paradigm as irrelevant

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the team shifts between deductive and inductive logic of inquiry

pros.claim: makes hidden assumptions explicit and defensible to reviewers
pros.example: a constructivist stance justifies thematic interpretation over frequency counts

cons.claim: over-theorizing paradigm can stall concrete design decisions
cons.example: weeks debating ontology while the timeline for data access closes

failure_modes: paradigm asserted but contradicted by chosen methods
paradigm used to excuse weak rigor
acceptance_tests: paradigm stated and consistent with the design family selected

nodes.definition: Decide among quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods design families based on question, paradigm, and the type of evidence required.
outputs: rationale linking question to evidence type

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when evidence requirement shifts from measuring magnitude to understanding meaning

pros.claim: frames the entire data and analysis pipeline
pros.example: choosing mixed-methods commits to both a sampling frame and a qualitative coding scheme

cons.claim: premature family lock forecloses better-fitting hybrid designs
cons.example: locking pure-quant before realizing the mechanism needs qualitative exploration

failure_modes: family chosen for researcher convenience not question fit
acceptance_tests: selected family supports the required evidence type
family choice traces to question typology and paradigm

nodes.definition: Specify a randomized experiment with manipulated independent variable, random assignment, and control to license causal inference.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when randomization becomes infeasible and design must degrade to quasi-experimental

pros.claim: strongest design for unbiased causal estimates
pros.example: random assignment balances confounders in expectation across arms

cons.claim: often infeasible or unethical for many real questions
cons.example: cannot randomly assign people to smoking to study lung disease

acceptance_tests: assignment is genuinely random and concealed
treatment and control differ only in the manipulated variable

nodes.definition: Design comparative studies without random assignment using controls such as nonequivalent groups, regression discontinuity, interrupted time series, or difference-in-differences.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an identifying assumption (parallel trends, no manipulation of running variable) is violated

pros.claim: enables causal estimates when randomization is impossible
pros.example: interrupted time series evaluates a policy enacted at a known date

cons.claim: identification rests on untestable assumptions about selection
cons.example: diff-in-diff fails if treated and control trends would have diverged anyway

failure_modes: selection bias mistaken for treatment effect
acceptance_tests: identification strategy named and its key assumption stated
selection mechanism addressed by a stated control

nodes.definition: Design non-interventional studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional correlational) that observe associations without manipulating variables.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an unmeasured confounder is identified that biases the association

pros.claim: feasible and ethical where experiments are not
pros.example: a cohort follows exposed and unexposed groups over time without intervening

cons.claim: association cannot be read as causation without strong assumptions
cons.example: reporting a correlation as if it proved a causal effect

acceptance_tests: key confounders enumerated and adjustment specified
causal language matches the design's inferential limits

nodes.definition: Design an in-depth, bounded study of one or a few cases using multiple data sources to investigate a phenomenon in its real-world context.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the case boundary proves untenable and must be redefined

pros.claim: captures context and mechanism in rich detail
pros.example: explains how a single organization adopted an innovation through interviews plus documents

cons.claim: findings generalize analytically, not statistically
cons.example: one firm's adoption path cannot be claimed for all firms

acceptance_tests: case explicitly bounded in time/place/unit
at least two independent data sources triangulated
revisit_triggers: selected case proves atypical for the proposition

nodes.definition: Design a survey to describe or relate variables in a population at one point in time via a structured instrument and a defined sampling frame.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when nonresponse bias threatens the representativeness of the snapshot

pros.claim: efficient breadth across large populations
pros.example: a national web survey estimates attitude prevalence quickly

cons.claim: cross-sectional timing precludes temporal/causal ordering
cons.example: cannot tell whether attitude preceded or followed behavior

acceptance_tests: sampling frame covers the target population
items pretested for clarity and single-barrel structure
revisit_triggers: construct coverage gap found in pretest

nodes.definition: Design prolonged immersive fieldwork to describe a culture-sharing group's practices and meanings from participants' perspectives.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when researcher positionality materially shifts the access or interpretation

pros.claim: reveals tacit cultural meaning unavailable to surveys
pros.example: prolonged immersion uncovers an unspoken workplace norm

cons.claim: time-intensive and entangled with researcher subjectivity
cons.example: months in the field with findings shaped by the observer's stance

acceptance_tests: engagement duration adequate for the cultural claim
reflexivity/positionality documented

nodes.definition: Design an inductive study that builds theory from data via iterative coding, constant comparison, and theoretical sampling until saturation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when categories stop changing, indicating saturation reached or mis-judged

pros.claim: generates theory tightly fitted to the data
pros.example: a substantive theory of patient coping emerges from interview coding

cons.claim: iterative design resists fixed timelines and pre-registration
cons.example: sample size cannot be fixed in advance because it depends on saturation

acceptance_tests: saturation defined operationally and evidenced
sampling driven by emerging theory not convenience

nodes.definition: Design intentional integration of quantitative and qualitative strands (convergent, explanatory-sequential, exploratory-sequential, embedded) with a defined point and purpose of integration.
inputs: question needing both magnitude and meaning

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the two strands produce divergent findings requiring re-integration

pros.claim: combines breadth and depth and enables triangulation
pros.example: survey magnitudes explained by follow-up interviews in an explanatory-sequential design

cons.claim: integration is hard and often degenerates into parallel reporting
cons.example: two studies stapled together with no joint inference

acceptance_tests: integration point and purpose explicitly specified
a joint display or meta-inference plan exists

nodes.definition: Decide the temporal structure of data collection (one-time cross-sectional vs repeated longitudinal/panel/cohort) to match the question's need for change or temporal ordering.
inputs: does the question concern change or ordering

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the question shifts from prevalence to change-over-time

pros.claim: longitudinal data establishes temporal precedence
pros.example: a panel measures attitude before and after an event to order cause and effect

cons.claim: longitudinal designs incur attrition and high cost
cons.example: a 5-wave panel loses a third of participants by the final wave

failure_modes: cross-sectional used for an inherently change question
acceptance_tests: temporal structure matches whether change/ordering is claimed
attrition plan present for longitudinal designs
revisit_triggers: question changes to require temporal ordering

nodes.definition: Design random selection (simple, stratified, cluster, systematic) from a defined frame so that population inference and sampling error are estimable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the sampling frame is found to undercover the target population

pros.claim: supports unbiased population inference and error estimates
pros.example: stratified random sampling guarantees subgroup representation with known probabilities

cons.claim: requires a complete frame and is costly to execute
cons.example: no usable frame exists for a hidden population

failure_modes: cluster design ignored in variance estimation
acceptance_tests: selection probabilities defined and nonzero for all units
frame coverage of target population assessed

nodes.definition: Design intentional nonrandom selection (purposive, theoretical, snowball, quota, maximum-variation) to capture information-rich cases for qualitative or theory-building aims.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when selection criteria no longer surface new information

pros.claim: targets information-rich cases for depth and theory
pros.example: maximum-variation sampling spans extreme cases to map a phenomenon's range

cons.claim: no basis for statistical generalization and selection bias risk
cons.example: snowball recruiting over-represents one social network

failure_modes: sampling logic disconnected from the question
acceptance_tests: selection criteria justified by the analytic purpose
sampling logic linked to saturation or variation goal

nodes.definition: Determine the sample size needed for adequate statistical power or qualitative saturation given effect size, alpha, and design effects.
contradictors: researcher who fixes N by convenience

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the assumed effect size proves implausible against pilot data

pros.claim: prevents underpowered, inconclusive studies
pros.example: an a-priori power analysis sets N to detect the smallest meaningful effect

cons.claim: depends on an assumed effect size that is often guessed
cons.example: optimistic effect-size assumption yields an underpowered study

failure_modes: post-hoc power used to interpret null results
design effect ignored in clustered samples
acceptance_tests: sample size derived from stated effect size, alpha, and power
design effect included for non-simple samples
revisit_triggers: pilot effect size differs from assumption

nodes.definition: Establish that observed effects are attributable to the studied variable by identifying and controlling threats (history, maturation, selection, regression, attrition, testing, instrumentation).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new plausible confound is identified after design lock

pros.claim: protects the core causal claim from alternative explanations
pros.example: randomization plus blinding neutralizes selection and expectancy threats

cons.claim: maximizing internal validity can reduce realism/external validity
cons.example: tight lab control makes the setting unlike the real context

acceptance_tests: each major threat has a stated control or acknowledged limitation
no uncontrolled threat plausibly produces the effect

nodes.definition: Assess and design for the generalizability of findings across populations, settings, times, and treatment variations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the study population diverges from the intended target of inference

pros.claim: clarifies to whom and where results apply
pros.example: a representative national sample supports population-level claims

cons.claim: strong generalization often trades against internal control
cons.example: field realism gained at the cost of confound control

acceptance_tests: generalization claim bounded to the sampled population/setting
boundary conditions explicitly stated

nodes.definition: Ensure that operationalized measures and manipulations actually represent the intended theoretical constructs.
contradictors: researcher who conflates measure with construct

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when convergent/discriminant evidence contradicts the assumed construct mapping

pros.claim: ensures the study measures what it claims to
pros.example: convergent and discriminant evidence confirms a scale taps the target construct

cons.claim: construct underrepresentation and method bias are easy to miss
cons.example: a single self-report item under-represents a multidimensional construct

acceptance_tests: each construct mapped to a justified operationalization
convergent/discriminant or manipulation-check evidence planned

nodes.definition: Ensure inferences about covariation are correct by controlling power, assumption violations, error rates, and analytic flexibility.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when assumptions are violated or analytic flexibility inflates false positives

pros.claim: guards against false-positive and false-negative conclusions
pros.example: pre-registration plus error-rate control limits fishing for significance

cons.claim: rigid pre-specification can miss genuine unexpected effects
cons.example: a strict plan cannot follow up a surprising but real pattern

failure_modes: underpowered test treated as evidence of no effect
acceptance_tests: analysis plan pre-specified with error-rate control
statistical assumptions checked and reported

nodes.definition: Design instruments and procedures that yield consistent, low-error measurements (internal consistency, test-retest, inter-rater) as a precondition for valid inference.
contradictors: researcher who assumes instruments are error-free

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reliability estimates fall below the threshold needed for the analysis

pros.claim: unreliable measures cap the validity of any conclusion
pros.example: poor inter-rater agreement is fixed via training before main coding

cons.claim: high reliability does not guarantee the right construct
cons.example: a precise instrument can consistently measure the wrong thing

acceptance_tests: reliability estimated and meets the pre-set threshold
rater agreement assessed before main coding

nodes.definition: Design the study to meet ethical principles and obtain institutional review board (IRB) approval, addressing consent, risk, privacy, and vulnerable populations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when procedures change in ways that alter participant risk or consent scope

pros.claim: protects participants and is a hard gate to data collection
pros.example: IRB approval is required before any human-subjects data is collected

cons.claim: review timelines and amendments can delay the study
cons.example: a protocol amendment for an added question delays fieldwork weeks

failure_modes: consent fails to cover actual data use
acceptance_tests: IRB approval obtained before data collection
consent scope covers all planned data uses

edges.why_related: the question typology constrains which epistemological stances are coherent
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligned stance avoids later method contradictions
edges.risk_of_conflict: picking a paradigm before the question forces a bad fit
edges.example: a causal question pushes toward post-positivism
edges.resolution_rule: resolve question typology before justifying paradigm

edges.why_related: the family must be chosen to answer the stated question
edges.benefit_of_coupling: family choice inherits the inference logic of the question
edges.risk_of_conflict: family chosen before the question yields mismatch
edges.example: relational question -> correlational or mixed family
edges.resolution_rule: finalize question typology before family lock

edges.why_related: paradigm sets epistemic constraints on admissible families
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring paradigm yields method-paradigm contradiction
edges.resolution_rule: reconcile paradigm before family selection

edges.why_related: experimental design is a quantitative-family specialization
edges.benefit_of_coupling: family decision scopes the specific design
edges.risk_of_conflict: specifying RCT outside a quant family is incoherent
edges.resolution_rule: select quantitative family before specifying an experiment

edges.why_related: quasi-experimental design is a quantitative-family specialization
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scopes identification strategy to the family
edges.risk_of_conflict: specifying without family lock risks rework
edges.example: quant causal family without randomization -> quasi
edges.resolution_rule: lock family before identification strategy

edges.why_related: observational design specializes the quantitative family
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligns association logic to the family
edges.risk_of_conflict: mismatch if family undecided
edges.resolution_rule: decide family before observational specifics

edges.why_related: survey is a quantitative-family specialization for description/relation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scopes instrument and frame to family
edges.risk_of_conflict: instrument built before family wastes effort
edges.resolution_rule: fix family before drafting the survey

edges.why_related: case study specializes the qualitative family
edges.risk_of_conflict: case design without family is unfocused
edges.resolution_rule: decide family before bounding the case

edges.why_related: ethnography specializes the qualitative family
edges.risk_of_conflict: fieldwork before family is premature
edges.resolution_rule: decide family before planning fieldwork

edges.why_related: grounded theory specializes the qualitative family
edges.risk_of_conflict: coding before family lacks grounding
edges.resolution_rule: decide family before iterative coding

edges.why_related: mixed-methods integrates strands chosen at the family level
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scopes integration to the chosen strands
edges.risk_of_conflict: integration before family is unspecified
edges.resolution_rule: decide family before integration design

edges.why_related: temporal structure is decided within the chosen family
edges.risk_of_conflict: timing before family is premature
edges.resolution_rule: fix family before temporal structure

edges.why_related: the experiment must not be finalized before its internal-validity threats are controlled
edges.risk_of_conflict: unvalidated design risks confounded results
edges.resolution_rule: control threats before finalizing the experiment

edges.why_related: quasi-experimental inference depends on controlling selection and history threats
edges.benefit_of_coupling: named controls license the causal estimate
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignored threats invalidate identification
edges.resolution_rule: resolve identifying threats before finalizing

edges.why_related: maximizing control tightens the setting and can reduce realism
edges.risk_of_conflict: optimizing one silently degrades the other
edges.example: tight lab control reduces ecological validity
edges.resolution_rule: set the priority by the study's primary inferential goal; document the tradeoff

edges.why_related: representative probability sampling underwrites population generalization
edges.benefit_of_coupling: representative frame supports the generalization claim
edges.risk_of_conflict: biased sampling caps external validity
edges.resolution_rule: establish representative sampling before claiming generalizability

edges.why_related: the family determines whether probability sampling is the appropriate strategy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligns sampling logic to inference needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: sampling chosen before family risks mismatch
edges.resolution_rule: decide family before sampling strategy

edges.why_related: qualitative/theory-building families call for nonprobability sampling
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligns purposive logic to the family
edges.risk_of_conflict: random sampling forced on qual aims wastes effort
edges.resolution_rule: decide family before nonprobability sampling logic

edges.why_related: probability and purposive logics optimize generalization vs information richness
edges.benefit_of_coupling: explicit choice avoids a hybrid that serves neither
edges.risk_of_conflict: mixing logics without rationale undermines both
edges.resolution_rule: choose the sampling logic that matches the inference goal; mixed designs must justify each strand

edges.why_related: design effects from the sampling plan feed the sample-size computation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correct design effect yields a valid N
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring clustering underpowers the study
edges.resolution_rule: finalize sampling design before computing sample size

edges.why_related: adequate power is a precondition for valid statistical conclusions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sufficient power controls Type II error
edges.risk_of_conflict: underpowered study yields unreliable conclusions
edges.example: power 0.8 supports detecting the target effect
edges.resolution_rule: set sample size for power before fixing the analysis claims

edges.why_related: the chosen sample size bounds the minimum detectable effect of the analysis
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming small effects beyond detectable bound misleads
edges.example: N caps the smallest reliably detectable effect
edges.resolution_rule: report the minimum detectable effect implied by N

edges.why_related: valid construct interpretation presupposes reliable measurement
edges.risk_of_conflict: unreliable measures cap construct validity
edges.resolution_rule: establish reliability before claiming construct validity

edges.why_related: measurement error reduces effective power and attenuates observed effects
edges.risk_of_conflict: unaccounted error biases conclusions toward null
edges.resolution_rule: account for measurement error in power and effect estimates

edges.why_related: operationalized constructs constrain admissible survey items
edges.risk_of_conflict: items drifting from constructs invalidate the survey
edges.example: each item maps to a defined construct
edges.resolution_rule: constrain item wording to the operationalized constructs

edges.why_related: the manipulation must validly instantiate the intended construct
edges.risk_of_conflict: an invalid manipulation tests the wrong construct
edges.example: manipulation-check item confirms the induced state
edges.resolution_rule: require a manipulation check tied to the construct

edges.why_related: temporal structure changes which internal-validity threats apply
edges.risk_of_conflict: cross-sectional timing invites reverse-causation threats
edges.resolution_rule: choose temporal structure to neutralize the dominant threat

edges.why_related: absence of manipulation limits the internal-validity controls available
edges.risk_of_conflict: reading association as causation is invalid
edges.resolution_rule: bound causal language to the design's control capacity

edges.why_related: ethical limits restrict admissible manipulations and assignment
edges.risk_of_conflict: unethical manipulation cannot proceed regardless of power
edges.example: cannot randomize people to a harmful exposure
edges.resolution_rule: ethics constraints dominate design optimization

edges.why_related: consent and vulnerable-population rules constrain recruitment
edges.risk_of_conflict: unconsented snowball recruiting breaches ethics
edges.example: snowball recruiting must still secure consent
edges.resolution_rule: recruitment must satisfy consent and protection rules

edges.why_related: immersive observation raises consent and privacy constraints
edges.risk_of_conflict: covert observation without consent is unethical
edges.resolution_rule: field consent and privacy rules constrain immersion

edges.why_related: the question and procedures must be defined enough to draft the IRB protocol
edges.risk_of_conflict: drafting IRB before procedures wastes review cycles
edges.resolution_rule: define procedures before drafting the IRB protocol

edges.why_related: both concern the credibility of the inferred relationship but at different layers
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clarifies they are distinct validity types
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them hides which threat applies
edges.example: a confound (internal) differs from a power gap (statistical)
edges.resolution_rule: keep the two validity types distinct in the design rationale

edges.why_related: single/few-case scope limits statistical generalization
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming statistical generalization from one case misleads
edges.example: one case generalizes to theory not population
edges.resolution_rule: frame case findings as analytic, not statistical, generalization

edges.why_related: theoretical sampling is the engine that drives grounded-theory data collection
edges.risk_of_conflict: fixed sampling breaks the inductive logic
edges.resolution_rule: tie sampling to emerging theory and saturation

edges.why_related: divergent strand findings can trigger re-examination of confound control
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded re-integration loops stall the study
edges.example: qual strand reveals an uncontrolled confound
edges.resolution_rule: revisit threat controls when strands diverge; stop after one re-integration unless new evidence appears

edges.why_related: a generalization target across subgroups can require revisiting sample size
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring subgroup needs underpowers comparisons
edges.resolution_rule: recompute N when subgroup generalization is required; stop when power targets are met

edges.why_related: construct operationalization should follow family selection to fit the evidence type
edges.risk_of_conflict: operationalizing before family forces rework
edges.resolution_rule: operationalize constructs after the family is chosen

resolution_order: identify the study's primary inferential goal
prioritize the validity type that goal demands
document the conceded validity as a limitation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the validity type required by the primary research aim dominates; the conceded type is reported as a bounded limitation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the study claims both strong causal and strong population inference simultaneously
conflict_axes.example: a tightly controlled lab experiment that cannot claim field generalizability

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing between representativeness and information-rich case selection
resolution_order: classify inference goal as generalization vs depth
select the sampling logic that serves it
justify any hybrid strand separately
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: generalization aims dominate toward probability sampling; depth/theory aims dominate toward purposive sampling
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if statistical generalization is claimed from a purposive sample
conflict_axes.example: random sampling for prevalence vs maximum-variation sampling for theory

conflict_axes.trigger: the question needs both magnitude and meaning but resources force a priority
resolution_order: decide whether magnitude or meaning is primary
prioritize that strand
use mixed methods only with an integration plan
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the evidence type the primary aim requires dominates; mixed methods is chosen only when integration is planned
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if both strands are run without an integration point
conflict_axes.example: measuring effect size vs understanding lived experience

conflict_axes.trigger: the most rigorous manipulation or assignment would harm or burden participants
resolution_order: assess participant risk
apply the least-burdensome design meeting the aim
escalate to IRB if rigor and ethics conflict
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: ethical constraints dominate design rigor without exception
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: any design feature that increases participant risk beyond minimal
conflict_axes.example: a powerful but harmful randomization that the IRB will not approve

conflict_axes.trigger: the design must choose between pre-specification and iterative adaptation
resolution_order: classify the aim as confirmatory vs exploratory
adopt fixed design for confirmatory and emergent for exploratory
document any deviation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: confirmatory aims dominate toward pre-specified designs; exploratory aims dominate toward emergent designs
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if confirmatory claims are made from an emergent, unregistered design
conflict_axes.example: pre-registered RCT vs saturation-driven grounded theory

conflict_axes.trigger: limited resources force a choice between many shallow cases and few deep ones
resolution_order: determine whether prevalence or mechanism is primary
allocate resources to breadth or depth accordingly
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: prevalence/generalization aims dominate toward breadth; mechanism/understanding aims dominate toward depth
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a depth design is used to claim prevalence
conflict_axes.example: a 2000-person survey vs three immersive case studies

conflict_axes.trigger: a highly reliable instrument may consistently measure the wrong construct
resolution_order: confirm the measure targets the intended construct
then optimize reliability of that measure
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: construct validity dominates: a reliable but invalid measure is rejected before reliability is optimized
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if reliability is reported without construct evidence
conflict_axes.example: a precise scale that measures a related but wrong construct

conflict_axes.trigger: the N needed for power exceeds recruitable participants
resolution_order: recompute minimum detectable effect at feasible N
decide whether the feasible study is worth running
consider design changes to gain power
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if feasible N cannot detect the smallest meaningful effect, the confirmatory claim is downgraded or the design is changed
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if an underpowered study is framed as confirmatory
conflict_axes.example: a rare-population study that cannot reach the required N

conflict_axes.trigger: temporal ordering needs longitudinal data but budget favors a snapshot
resolution_order: determine whether the claim requires change or ordering
fund longitudinal only if ordering is essential
otherwise bound the claim to cross-sectional inference
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if causal ordering is claimed, longitudinal structure dominates; otherwise cost favors cross-sectional with bounded claims
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if temporal/causal ordering is claimed from cross-sectional data
conflict_axes.example: a panel study versus a one-time correlational survey

edge_cases.trigger: a causal claim drawn from a correlational/observational design
edge_cases.failure_mode: confounding or reverse causation read as a causal effect
edge_cases.example: reporting that X causes Y from a cross-sectional correlation
edge_cases.detection_method: check causal language against the design's identification capacity
resolution: add an identification strategy or longitudinal data

edge_cases.trigger: the chosen design cannot answer the stated question
edge_cases.failure_mode: un-interpretable results relative to the aim
edge_cases.example: a descriptive survey used to answer a causal question
edge_cases.detection_method: verify each aim maps to a design whose inference logic supports it
resolution: or reframe the question to match the feasible design

edge_cases.trigger: allocation concealment fails or assignment is non-random in practice
edge_cases.failure_mode: selection bias reintroduced into an experiment
edge_cases.example: clinicians steer sicker patients to treatment
edge_cases.detection_method: audit randomization logs and baseline balance across arms
resolution: reanalyze as quasi-experimental with selection controls

edge_cases.trigger: a non-significant result from an underpowered study is read as no effect
edge_cases.failure_mode: Type II error mistaken for evidence of absence
edge_cases.example: declaring no effect from an N=20 study
edge_cases.detection_method: compare achieved power and minimum detectable effect to the claim
resolution: treat as inconclusive rather than null

edge_cases.trigger: the sampling frame omits parts of the target population
edge_cases.example: a landline frame missing mobile-only households
edge_cases.detection_method: compare frame coverage against population benchmarks
resolution: apply coverage weighting and bound the claim

edge_cases.example: stopping interviews while new codes still emerge
edge_cases.detection_method: track new-code rate across recent data increments

edge_cases.trigger: two strands run with no integration point or joint inference
edge_cases.failure_mode: parallel reporting masquerading as mixed methods
edge_cases.example: a quant chapter and a qual chapter never connected
edge_cases.detection_method: check for a specified integration point and joint display
resolution: define the integration point and purpose
produce a joint display or meta-inference

edge_cases.trigger: a measure under-represents a multidimensional construct
edge_cases.example: a single item used for a broad attitude construct
edge_cases.detection_method: check construct definition against item/content coverage

edge_cases.trigger: data collected before IRB approval or beyond consent scope
edge_cases.failure_mode: ethical breach invalidating use of the data
edge_cases.example: surveying participants before approval is granted
edge_cases.detection_method: verify approval and consent-scope timestamps precede collection
resolution: seek approval/amendment; may require discarding non-compliant data

edge_cases.trigger: differential dropout across waves or arms
edge_cases.example: sicker participants drop out of the treatment arm
edge_cases.detection_method: compare attrition rates and baseline profiles across groups/waves
resolution: bound the claim to completers with stated caveats

edge_cases.trigger: stated paradigm contradicts the chosen methods
edge_cases.example: a constructivist stance paired with a pure frequency survey claim
edge_cases.detection_method: check paradigm-method consistency in the rationale
resolution: align the paradigm or the method

edge_cases.trigger: convenience sampling labeled as purposive and used to generalize
edge_cases.example: recruiting whoever is available and calling it purposive
edge_cases.detection_method: check selection criteria against the stated analytic purpose
resolution: limit claims to analytic, not statistical, generalization

workflow.objective: fix the research question typology, unit of analysis, and competency questions
acceptance_tests: each aim maps to a design whose inference logic supports it
unit of analysis stated
workflow.do_first_because: question alignment is the highest-coupling foundation every design choice inherits

workflow.objective: justify the paradigm and select the quant/qual/mixed design family
acceptance_tests: paradigm consistent with selected family
family supports the required evidence type
workflow.do_first_because: family selection scopes every later design, sampling, and validity choice

outputs: specified design with its inference logic
acceptance_tests: the specified design's inference logic answers the question
design feasibility confirmed
workflow.do_first_because: the specific design must exist before validity and sampling can be tailored to it

workflow.objective: decide cross-sectional vs longitudinal structure and wave schedule
acceptance_tests: temporal structure matches whether change/ordering is claimed
attrition plan present if longitudinal
workflow.do_first_because: temporal structure interacts with sampling and validity and must be set before they are finalized

workflow.objective: operationalize constructs and establish reliable instrumentation
acceptance_tests: each construct mapped to a justified operationalization
reliability meets the pre-set threshold
workflow.do_first_because: unreliable or invalid measures cap every downstream conclusion

workflow.objective: select the sampling strategy and determine size/power or saturation
acceptance_tests: sampling logic matches the inference goal
sample size derived from effect size, alpha, power or saturation justified
workflow.do_first_because: sampling and power must be fixed before validity claims and ethics can be finalized

workflow.objective: identify and control validity threats and pre-specify the analysis
acceptance_tests: each major threat has a control or stated limitation
analysis plan pre-specified with error-rate control
workflow.do_first_because: validity threats must be controlled before the design can be locked

workflow.objective: obtain IRB approval and finalize consent and data-protection plans
acceptance_tests: IRB approval obtained before any data collection
consent scope covers all planned data uses
workflow.do_first_because: ethics is an irreversible gate; no data may be collected before approval

workflow.objective: validate end-to-end design coherence and lock the protocol
acceptance_tests: every aim traces to a controlled, ethical, powered design
all high-risk nodes human-reviewed
workflow.do_first_because: locking requires all dependency, validity, and ethics gates to have passed

priority_rationale.notes: root alignment all design choices inherit
scopes all specific designs, sampling, and validity
threat control gates all causal designs
strongest causal design, high risk if mis-specified
temporal structure interacts with sampling and validity
integration design needs strands defined first
depends on internal validity and sampling

dominance_rules.trigger: a more rigorous design increases participant risk
dominance_rules.rule: ethical constraints dominate design rigor without exception
dominance_rules.required_action: block the design until an ethics-compliant alternative is found
dominance_rules.example: reject a harmful but powerful randomization

dominance_rules.trigger: a faster design path raises the risk of invalid inference
dominance_rules.rule: never accept a time saving that compromises a validity gate
dominance_rules.required_action: require the validity gate to pass before proceeding
dominance_rules.example: skip-the-pretest shortcut rejected because reliability is unverified

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value design choice is requested before its prerequisite is fixed
dominance_rules.required_action: complete the prerequisite node before the dependent one
dominance_rules.example: do not finalize sampling before the family is selected

dominance_rules.trigger: a preferred method is chosen before the question is settled
dominance_rules.rule: the research question's inference need dominates method familiarity
dominance_rules.required_action: re-select the design to fit the question
dominance_rules.example: abandon a favored survey when the question is causal

dominance_rules.trigger: a reliable measure may not capture the intended construct
dominance_rules.required_action: confirm the measure targets the construct before optimizing reliability
dominance_rules.example: reject a precise but off-construct scale

dominance_rules.trigger: internal and external validity cannot both be maximized
dominance_rules.rule: the validity type the primary aim requires dominates
dominance_rules.required_action: prioritize that type and report the other as a bounded limitation
dominance_rules.example: lab control prioritized for a causal mechanism study

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible design decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automated acceptance for high-risk/irreversible nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: route the decision to human review before lock
dominance_rules.example: IRB and irreversible procedural choices require human sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: feasible N cannot detect the smallest meaningful effect
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade to inconclusive or change the design
dominance_rules.example: reframe an underpowered study as exploratory

dominance_rules.trigger: numeric estimates are presented without eligible evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: label estimates heuristic unless eligible data supports otherwise
dominance_rules.example: do not label a guessed effect size as observed

dominance_rules.trigger: a design is about to be locked before validation passes
dominance_rules.required_action: block hard lock until all validity and ethics gates pass
dominance_rules.example: no protocol lock before the threat-control matrix is complete

dominance_rules.trigger: two strands are reported without integration
dominance_rules.rule: integration dominates parallel reporting in mixed methods
dominance_rules.required_action: require an integration point and joint inference
dominance_rules.example: add a joint display before claiming mixed-methods findings

dominance_rules.trigger: a design object is added without traceability to a question or source
dominance_rules.required_action: link each design element to a competency question and source
dominance_rules.example: drop a design feature that answers no stated aim

anti_rework_rules.rule: settle the research question typology before selecting any design
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a design built on the wrong question forces a full redesign
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: design changed after the question is reframed
anti_rework_rules.example: RCT planned then dropped when the question turned descriptive

anti_rework_rules.rule: justify the paradigm before locking the design family
anti_rework_rules.rationale: paradigm-method contradictions discovered late force rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: family chosen that contradicts the stated paradigm
anti_rework_rules.example: constructivist stance bolted onto a frequency-only survey

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the design family before specifying a within-family design
anti_rework_rules.rationale: specifying a design before the family wastes detailed work
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: detailed protocol drafted before the family is decided
anti_rework_rules.example: survey instrument built before deciding quant vs mixed

anti_rework_rules.rule: finalize the specific design before the sampling plan
anti_rework_rules.rationale: sampling tuned to a design that later changes is wasted
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: sampling plan written before the design is settled
anti_rework_rules.example: power computed for an experiment later changed to observational

anti_rework_rules.rule: finalize the sampling design before computing sample size
anti_rework_rules.rationale: design effects from sampling change the required N
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: N computed before clustering is known
anti_rework_rules.example: simple-random N used for a cluster sample

anti_rework_rules.rationale: reliability of an off-construct measure is wasted effort
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: reliability tuned before the construct mapping is set
anti_rework_rules.example: optimizing a scale that measures the wrong construct

anti_rework_rules.rule: control internal-validity threats before locking the design
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an uncontrolled threat discovered post-lock voids results
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: design locked while a plausible confound remains
anti_rework_rules.example: confound found after data collection began

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix sample size and power before pre-specifying the analysis claims
anti_rework_rules.rationale: analysis claims beyond detectable effect mislead
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: analysis plan promises effects N cannot detect
anti_rework_rules.example: claiming small-effect detection from a tiny sample

anti_rework_rules.rule: obtain IRB approval before any data collection
anti_rework_rules.rationale: data collected before approval may be unusable and unethical
anti_rework_rules.example: pilot data gathered pre-approval and later discarded

anti_rework_rules.rule: define the integration point before locking a mixed-methods design
anti_rework_rules.rationale: strands without integration require re-running for joint inference
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: mixed-methods locked with no joint display
anti_rework_rules.example: two unconnected strands reported as mixed methods

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete the traceability matrix before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: untraceable design elements cause rework at review
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: hard lock attempted with incomplete traceability
anti_rework_rules.example: a design feature with no linked aim survives to lock

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or design review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk_score and irreversibility
action: sort defects by risk and reversibility
acceptance_tests: high-risk defects scheduled first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only low-risk below tolerance

iteration_protocol.detection: trace edges from the changed node
acceptance_tests: all downstream dependents identified

iteration_protocol.detection: map defect type to repair owner via repair_routing
acceptance_tests: defect routed to a valid owner

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and formula checks
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence about a design choice arrives
iteration_protocol.detection: compare posterior delta to revisit threshold
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed within tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a dependency cycle or invalid edge is detected
acceptance_tests: dependency graph acyclic
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no cycles and all endpoints valid

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changes after a downstream lock
acceptance_tests: dependent locks downgraded

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible defect cannot be auto-repaired
acceptance_tests: high-risk defect has a review owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new design version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version baseline
acceptance_tests: no validity regression versus baseline
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no regression or accepted with record

human_review_required_for: hard lock of the design protocol

checks.repair_action: modeled internal-vs-external tension as a conflict edge, not a dependency
recomputed all derived fields via formula script

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked design change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when evidence label is revised
human_approval_required_for: hard lock of the design protocol
